subject: Government
title: Basic Concepts and Definitions of Government
outline: Government as an institution of the state
Government as a process or art of governing
Government as an academic field of study
Organs of government: legislature, executive, judiciary
Levels of government: federal, state, local
Why the study of government matters to the citizen

modules.title: What Government Means
modules.html:
Government is the machinery through which the will of the state is formulated, expressed and carried out. Because the state is an abstract legal person, it cannot act on its own; it needs living human beings organised into offices and institutions. Those offices, taken together, are the government.

Scholars use the word in three distinct senses, and every examination question turns on knowing which sense is meant:

SenseMeaningIllustration
As an institutionThe set of organs and offices established by the constitution to exercise state power.The National Assembly, the Presidency and the Supreme Court of Nigeria.
As a processThe activity or art of governing — making, applying and enforcing rules.The passage of the annual Appropriation Bill from first reading to presidential assent.
As a field of studyThe academic discipline that examines political institutions and behaviour.Government offered as a WASSCE subject; Political Science in a university.

Notice that the first sense answers who, the second answers how, and the third answers what is studied. A candidate who defines government only as “the people in power” captures just one third of the concept.

examples.q: A student writes: 'Government is the President and his ministers.' Correct the answer.
examples.a: The statement is incomplete. It describes only part of the executive organ. Government as an institution includes the legislature and judiciary as well; and government also means the process of governing and an academic discipline.

modules.title: Functions of Government
modules.html:
Governments everywhere perform a recognisable core of functions. Learn them under two headings.

Primary (traditional) functions — the state cannot survive without them:

  • Maintenance of law and order through the police, courts and prisons.
  • Defence of territory from external aggression through the armed forces.
  • Administration of justice by an impartial judiciary.
  • Conduct of external relations — diplomacy, treaties, membership of the UN, AU and ECOWAS.
  • Raising revenue by taxation and spending it through a budget.

Secondary (welfare or service) functions — expanded greatly in the twentieth century:

  • Provision of education, health care, water and electricity.
  • Construction of roads, bridges, ports and other infrastructure.
  • Regulation of the economy: monetary policy, price control, consumer protection.
  • Social security, pensions and disaster relief.

The balance between the two determines the character of a state. A state limited to primary functions is often called a laissez-faire or night-watchman state; one that carries heavy secondary functions is a welfare state.

examples.q: Classify: (i) fighting Boko Haram; (ii) building the Lagos–Ibadan expressway.
examples.a: (i) A primary function – defence and maintenance of internal security. (ii) A secondary or welfare function – provision of infrastructure.

modules.title: The Three Organs of Government
modules.html:
Every modern government is analysed through three organs. The distinction was systematised by Baron de Montesquieu in The Spirit of the Laws (1748).

OrganCore dutyNigerian exampleHead
LegislatureMakes, amends and repeals laws; approves the budget; oversees the executive.National Assembly (Senate + House of Representatives)Senate President / Speaker
ExecutiveImplements and enforces laws; formulates policy; conducts foreign relations.The President, Vice-President, ministers and the civil serviceThe President
JudiciaryInterprets the law, settles disputes, protects fundamental rights, reviews legislation.Supreme Court, Court of Appeal, Federal and State High CourtsChief Justice of Nigeria

The legislature is described as the first estate of the realm because law must exist before it can be executed or interpreted. The judiciary is called the watchdog of the constitution because through judicial review it can declare an act of the legislature or the executive ultra vires (beyond its powers) and therefore null and void.

examples.q: Which organ exercises the power of judicial review and what does it mean?
examples.a: The judiciary. Judicial review is the power of the courts to examine laws and executive acts and to nullify those that conflict with the constitution.

modules.title: Levels of Government and Related Concepts
modules.html:
In a federation such as Nigeria, government also exists at levels. The 1999 Constitution recognises the federal government (36 states plus the FCT), state governments, and 774 local government councils. Powers are shared through the Exclusive Legislative List (federal only), the Concurrent List (federal and state) and the Residual List (state only).

Three related words are often confused:

  • Politics — the struggle to acquire, retain and use governmental power; famously described by Harold Lasswell as “who gets what, when and how”.
  • Policy — a deliberate course of action adopted by government, e.g. the Universal Basic Education policy.
  • Public administration — the machinery, personnel and procedures by which policy is carried out day to day.

Why study government? It produces informed citizens who understand their rights and duties, trains future administrators and leaders, promotes political stability by explaining institutions, and equips students for careers in law, diplomacy, journalism and public service.

examples.q: Distinguish between politics and public administration in one sentence each.
examples.a: Politics is the competitive struggle over who exercises state power and for what ends; public administration is the neutral, professional execution of the decisions that emerge from that struggle.

quiz.q: Government as an institution refers to
options: The organs and offices that exercise state power
quiz.solution: As an institution, government is the set of established organs – legislature, executive, judiciary.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT an organ of government?
quiz.solution: The electorate is the body of voters, not an organ of government.

quiz.q: The organ of government that interprets the law is the
quiz.solution: Interpretation of law is the constitutional duty of the judiciary.

quiz.q: Montesquieu's doctrine of separation of powers appeared in
quiz.solution: Montesquieu published The Spirit of the Laws in 1748.

quiz.q: The primary function of government is best illustrated by
quiz.solution: Law and order is a traditional or primary function.

quiz.q: A state that limits itself to defence, law and order is described as a
quiz.solution: The laissez-faire or night-watchman state performs only minimal functions.

options: The activity of making and enforcing rules
quiz.solution: As a process, government is the art or activity of governing.

quiz.q: Which body approves the annual budget in Nigeria?
quiz.solution: Approval of the Appropriation Bill is a legislative function.

quiz.q: The legislature is often called the
quiz.solution: The legislature is the first estate because law precedes execution and interpretation.

quiz.q: Judicial review enables the courts to
quiz.solution: Judicial review nullifies acts that are ultra vires the constitution.

options: Who gets what, when and how
quiz.solution: Lasswell's classic formulation is 'who gets what, when and how'.

quiz.q: Nigeria operates how many levels of government?
quiz.solution: Federal, state and local government make three levels.

quiz.q: Matters on which only the Federal Government may legislate are on the
quiz.solution: The Exclusive Legislative List is reserved to the Federal Government.

quiz.q: The number of local government councils recognised by the 1999 Constitution is
quiz.solution: There are 774 constitutionally recognised local government areas.

quiz.q: A deliberate course of action adopted by government is called
quiz.solution: That is the definition of a public policy.

quiz.q: Conduct of foreign relations belongs to which organ?
quiz.solution: Diplomacy and treaty-making are executive functions, though treaties may need legislative ratification.
